77618.subject: Not Your Entropy, Not Your Coins
77618.body:
Modern Alchemy 

Автор: Jake ₿artolo


Автор: Jake ₿artolo

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/your-entropy-coins-jake-artolo-oc5qe?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BuPKETkFaRO6%2FGuS1aXmkHw%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2vvs9fvsz2tYo1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~msydjap1~cu-null-null&eid=fz96fz-msydjap1-cu
  
What does it mean for something to be truly random? How secure is it to hold your crypto on a self-custodial hardware wallet, and what are you still trusting when you do? The Coldcard attack prompted me to ask these questions and challenge several assumptions I had made. In this case, a broken random number generator sat inside the most trusted hardware wallet in Bitcoin for 5 years, and it did not occur to most people, including me, to ask whether the entropy was real. What bothers me now is not the device. It is the shape of the question. If I stopped examining that assumption, which others have I stopped examining. What happened In March 2021, a commit changed how Coldcard produced randomness. The device stopped drawing from its hardware random number generator and fell back to a software substitute seeded with chip data that was never secret. Users were told their seed was one of more possibilities than there are atoms in the universe. It was actually one of about a trillion, which is a weekend on a gaming PC. On 30 July 2026, in 41 minutes, attackers swept over a thousand Bitcoin from more than a thousand addresses, and further waves followed. Galaxy Research’s 14 August figure is 1,778 BTC confirmed, around $112 million, with an upper estimate including unconfirmed cases of 2,417 BTC, or roughly $153 million. Most of it has not moved. The coins had been dormant for an average of just over 3 years, so the people hit were mostly long-term holders who had done the thing they were told to do and then stopped thinking about it. Updating the firmware does not help them. The seed was born weak and stays weak. Why nobody saw it A generator that works produces output you cannot distinguish from noise, and a generator that is broken produces output you cannot distinguish from noise. There is no symptom, no error, no anomaly. The device boots, shows you 24 words, and behaves exactly as it did the day before. Coldcard’s firmware was public the entire time and anyone could read it. That has been the load-bearing argument for hardware wallets for a decade and it deserves stating precisely. Open source is permission to look, which is a different thing from evidence that anyone looked. The foreshadowing In December 2020, a researcher raised the question of whether a hardware wallet vendor could deliberately weaken seed generation and collect later. Rodolfo Novak, Coinkite
